verdict.rationale: Independent users credit Babylon.js with strong backwards compatibility and very good documentation, especially compared with Three.js, and it offers TypeScript IntelliSense. Its shareable Playground, llms.txt files and large npm footprint suggest a sizable public example corpus. However, nothing directly shows that LLM-generated Babylon code works on the first try, its docs are client-rendered with no .md mirrors, and one user reports little active community outside Microsoft-run channels. Missing for 10: hands-on evidence of LLM first-try success, evidence of abundant third-party public examples, LLM-friendly markdown doc mirrors.
